title: Flexible Flows for Biological Sequence Design
abstract: arXiv:2606.10543v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Designing functional biological sequences requires navigating vast discrete spaces under strict evolutionary and biophysical constraints. Discrete Flow Matching (DFM) offers a generative framework over such spaces, but existing approaches rely on biologically uninformative couplings and offer limited flexibility for variable-length sequence generation and fine-grained control. We propose a structured coupling that encodes domain-specific preferences among sequence elements, biasing the source distribution toward plausible regions without modifying the flow objective or training procedure. Building on this, we introduce a latent edit-based rate parameterization that models variable-length generation via edit operations conditioned on a shared global latent, akin to a latent variable model, while remaining tractable. translated_title: 面向生物序列设计的灵活流模型
translated_abstract: 设计功能性生物序列需要在严格的进化与生物物理约束下探索广阔的离散空间。离散流匹配为这类空间提供了一种生成式框架，但现有方法依赖于缺乏生物学信息的耦合方式，并且在变长序列生成和细粒度控制方面灵活性有限。我们提出了一种结构化耦合方法，在序列元素之间编码领域特定偏好，使源分布偏向合理的区域，而无需修改流的目标函数或训练过程。在此基础上，我们引入了一种基于潜变量的编辑式速率参数化方法，通过以共享全局潜变量为条件的编辑操作来建模变长序列生成，类似于潜变量模型，同时保持可处理性。我们还进一步引入了一种潜在无分类器引导机制，能够在连续潜空间中连贯地引导生成过程。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个面向生物序列设计的灵活离散流匹配框架，通过编码生物学偏好的结构化耦合、基于共享潜变量的编辑式速率参数化实现变长序列生成，以及潜在无分类器引导机制实现连贯且细粒度的生成控制。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a flexible Discrete Flow Matching framework for biological sequence design, featuring structured couplings that encode domain-specific biological preferences, a latent edit-based rate parameterization for variable-length sequence generation conditioned on a shared global latent, and a latent classifier-free guidance mechanism for coherent and fine-grained generation control.
